title: Working Copy Status
stagingNotice: No staging needed. Changes are automatically included in this commit when you save files.
gitStagingNotice: Three stages: git add → staged → git commit. Direct git operations are not recommended as jj manages them internally.

divergent.title: Divergent Change Detected
divergent.desc: The same change ID has diverged into multiple commits:
divergent.explanation: This commonly occurs when describe and auto-snapshot happen simultaneously. Git has no equivalent concept (jj-specific state).
divergent.method1Step1: 1. Check jj log to find which one is an ancestor of @ (keep that one)
divergent.method1Step2: 2. Verify with jj diff --from @ --to COMMIT_ID (if no + lines, WC has everything)
divergent.method1Step3: 3. If there are + lines, import with jj restore --from COMMIT_ID path
divergent.method1Step4: 4. jj abandon -r COMMIT_ID (use commit ID, not change ID — that would abandon both)
divergent.method2Title: Method 2: Restore to before the divergence
divergent.method2Desc: Find the operation before divergence in op log and restore to that point. Reliable, but all subsequent operations are also rolled back.

unstaged.title: There are unstaged changes
unstaged.gitRestorePath: Discard unstaged changes. Staged changes remain.
unstaged.jjRestorePath: Restore the specified file to the parent commit's state. No staged/unstaged distinction, so this is all you need.
unstaged.jjRestoreAll: Restore all files to the parent's state (equivalent to git checkout .).

staged.title: Staged changes only
staged.jjNoteDesc: Already committed in jj (working copy = commit). To move to the next commit:
staged.jjNewDesc: Finalize the current working copy and create a new empty commit.

wcChanges.title: Working copy has changes ({{count}} files)
wcChanges.moveForwardDesc: Finalize changes and create a new commit
wcChanges.squashToParentDesc: Absorb changes into the parent commit

undoVsRestore.title: jj undo vs jj restore
undoVsRestore.undoDesc: Undo the entire previous jj command (operation). Rolls back at the operation level: rebase, describe, new, etc.
undoVsRestore.undoExample4: # Back to the state before rebase
undoVsRestore.undoGit: git equivalent: git reflog + git reset
undoVsRestore.restoreDesc: Restore specific file contents from another revision. Only file contents change — the operation log is unaffected.
undoVsRestore.restoreExample2: # Only app.ts is restored to parent's state
undoVsRestore.restoreExample4: # Restore all files to parent's state
undoVsRestore.restoreGit: git equivalent: git restore / git checkout --

opComp.title: Operation Comparison: If you do this, this happens
opComp.subtitle: How jj and git commands differ for the same task. jj simplifies complex git operations.

jj.desc: Save files → automatically reflected in the commit. No staging needed. jj always takes snapshots.

git.desc: Stage with git add → finalize with git commit. Two steps required.

jj.desc: Create an empty commit on top of the current working copy. In git, empty commits require --allow-empty.

git.desc: Empty commits are a special operation. Normally you stage changes then commit.

jj.desc: Interactively split one commit into two. Select changes interactively.

git.desc: rebase -i to edit → reset → partial add → multiple commits. Many steps required.

jj.desc: Merge working copy changes into the parent commit. Equivalent to git's amend + add.

git.desc: Stage with add → rewrite the last commit with --amend.

jj.desc: Jump directly to a past commit and edit it. The working copy becomes that commit.

git.desc: Mark as edit in rebase -i → stop at that commit → modify → git rebase --continue.

jj.desc: Move any commit to a different parent. Conflicts are recorded as commits without interrupting (can be resolved later).

git.desc: Stops on conflict. Must resolve → git rebase --continue repeatedly.

jj.desc: bookmark = git's branch. In jj, you can develop without branches (anonymous branch style).

git.desc: Branches are essential. Without a branch, commits become orphaned (detached HEAD).

jj.desc: Create a new commit with multiple parents. jj new accepts any number of parents.

git.desc: Merge two branches. Conflicts must be resolved. Octopus merge is possible but rare.

jj.desc: Restore a file to the parent commit's state. For all files: jj restore --from @-. One command since there's no staging concept.

git.desc: Reverts unstaged changes. To revert staged, you need git restore --staged first. Two steps.

jj.desc: Undo at the operation level. jj undo reverts the last operation. op restore restores to any point in time.

git.desc: reset (revert history), revert (new commit to undo), reflog (restore from reference log). Different tools for different needs.
